missing: This tab has no RabbitMQ connection.
connectionGone: The RabbitMQ connection of this tab was deleted or is no longer shared with you.
renderError: This RabbitMQ view could not be drawn.
readOnly: Read-only access: publishing and other changes need write access to this connection.

sidebar.deleteDescription: The connection is removed from PatchMan (on every backend it was saved to). Nothing changes on the RabbitMQ server.

dialog.description: PatchMan talks to RabbitMQ through its management API, and over AMQP for live tails, stream reads and moving messages. The password is encrypted at rest.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.urlHelp: The address of the RabbitMQ management UI, usually port 15672 (e.g. http://rabbit.example.com:15672).
dialog.userHelp: The user needs the management tag (or monitoring / administrator to see nodes). PatchMan can only do what this user is allowed to do on each vhost.
dialog.backendLocalDesc: Requests go out from your machine (VPN, internal network).
dialog.backendRemoteDesc: Requests go out from the PatchMan server.
dialog.backendNote: The connection is saved on both backends; this picks which one runs it by default.
dialog.defaultVhost: Default vhost (used for the AMQP check)
dialog.amqpHelp: Only needed when AMQP isn't on the management host at 5672 (5671 with TLS).
dialog.amqpOk: AMQP works too: live tail, stream reads and moving messages are available.
dialog.amqpFailed: AMQP did not connect, so live tail, stream reads and moving messages won't work (everything else does): {{error}}

share.title: Share "{{name}}"
share.description: Give people or teams access to this RabbitMQ connection. Read: view, peek and tail. Write: also publish, purge, move, create and delete.
share.identityWarning: People you share with act as this connection's RabbitMQ user — the password itself is never shown to them.

rates.none: This broker keeps no message rate statistics (rates_mode is none or stats are disabled), so rates and charts are empty.

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.name: Node
nodes.alarmHint: While a memory or disk alarm is on, RabbitMQ blocks every publishing connection.
nodes.unavailable: Node details need the monitoring or administrator tag.

queue.purgeDescription: Deletes the ready messages ({{count}}) for good. Unacknowledged messages stay with their consumers.
queue.deleteDescription: The queue and every message in it are deleted. Producers that publish to it will have their messages dropped or returned.
queue.ifUnused: Only if it has no consumers
queue.noConditional: RabbitMQ can't make deleting a {{type}} queue conditional on it being empty — check the messages and consumers first.

queues.name: Name
queues.noConsumer: Messages are waiting but no consumer is attached.

exchange.defaultNote: The default exchange routes a message straight to the queue whose name is the routing key. Its bindings are implicit and can't be changed.
exchange.deleteDescription: The exchange and its bindings are deleted; messages published to it afterwards fail.

bindings.unbindDescription: Messages from "{{source}}" with key "{{key}}" will no longer arrive here.
bindings.defaultNote: Every queue is also bound to the default exchange with its own name as the routing key.

conn.closeDescription: "{{name}}" is disconnected at once; a well-behaved client reconnects. Its unacknowledged messages go back to their queues.
conn.unlimitedPrefetch: Unlimited prefetch: the consumer may be flooded with messages.

messages.requeueNote: Messages are read and put back in place. RabbitMQ marks them "redelivered", and while you read them a consumer can't take them.
messages.streamNote: This is a stream: messages are read from an offset and nothing changes on the queue.
messages.limitWarning: This RabbitMQ {{version}} quorum queue has a delivery limit of {{limit}}: every read counts as a delivery, and a message read that many times is {{dlx}}.
messages.dropped: dropped (the queue has no dead-letter exchange)
messages.removeDescription: The messages are taken off the queue and acknowledged — they are gone for good. You'll see them here once.

publish.directNote: Published through the default exchange, straight to this queue.
publish.routed: Published and routed to at least one queue.
publish.unrouted: Published, but no queue matched — the message was dropped (or returned).

move.title: Move messages from "{{name}}"
move.description: Typical use: send dead-lettered messages back to be processed again.
move.originDesc: Each message goes back to the exchange and routing key it was dead-lettered from (x-death header).
move.exchangeDesc: Publish to an exchange with a routing key (empty = keep each message's key).
move.note: Each message is published, confirmed, then removed from this queue. If the move is interrupted one message may end up in both places — never in neither.

tail.note: A temporary queue bound to this exchange receives copies of new messages while the tail runs; your queues are not touched. The RabbitMQ user needs the configure permission on the vhost.
tail.noDefault: The default exchange can't be tailed. Pick a named exchange.
tail.idle: Start the tail to watch messages arrive.

topology.focus: Focus on a queue or exchange…
topology.empty: Nothing to show in this vhost.

dialogs.argsInvalid: Arguments must be a JSON object.
dialogs.name: Name
dialogs.newQueueDesc: Quorum queues are replicated and the safe default; classic queues are lighter; streams keep messages for replay.
dialogs.newExchangeDesc: Exchanges route published messages to queues through bindings.
dialogs.ex_topic: Routing keys match patterns: * = one word, # = any number of words.
dialogs.ex_direct: The routing key must equal the binding key.
dialogs.ex_fanout: Every bound queue gets every message; keys are ignored.
dialogs.ex_headers: Routes on message headers instead of the routing key.
dialogs.newBindingDesc: Route messages from an exchange to a queue or another exchange.
dialogs.topicHelp: * matches one word, # matches zero or more (e.g. order.*.created, audit.#).
